title: Terminal-proof discipline woven into agent framework
bullets: Each agent turn now opens with a proof-over-appearance directive through the existing governor chain, so responses favor demonstrated verification over confident claims.
Terminal-proof discipline is now distributed across the Four Laws, verification standards, and execution guidance, so the same rigor applies in every workflow instead of living in a standalone block.
A hard Final-State Verification gate now requires every required artifact and check to pass before any completion claim, catching missing outputs and unintended changes.

title: Runtime surface audit maps six-runner gaps
bullets: You now have an evidence-backed map of every doc and script still enumerating three runtimes (Claude, Codex, OpenCode) instead of the six actually shipped, with 20+ sites identified.

You can see which gaps are hard (root contracts, advisor runtime enum, validation allowlists) versus soft (secondary skill docs, SYNC.md counts, doctor docs), separated from clean surfaces like sk-code's detection.

New guidance covers clear plain-language writing, honest recommendations, and an Ask-then-Do framing for complex requests.
The deep Codex voice spec was reconciled with the root rules so the two stay in sync instead of drifting.
The rules tune delivery without sacrificing rigor, avoiding over-constrained or timid AI voice.

title: AGENTS.md bloat audit and cleanup

Fixed all seven broken constitutional/*.md links and removed duplicate text so framework guidance now resolves correctly instead of referencing dead paths.

Removed obsolete Fable and Open Design dispatch rules, repaired the runtime agent-directory table (adding the missing Cursor and Devin rows), and collapsed one section into a pointer while preserving every normative constraint.

Rewrote the executor-delegation scorer to build its alias table from the hub's mode-registry instead of a top-level family filter, so runtime dispatch still resolves both executor kinds after the fold.
Preserved existing dispatch behavior and skill names, since the change relocates and re-registers the skills without altering dispatch semantics.

title: Codex CLI revival: fail-closed dispatch, hooks, agents
bullets: Use Codex CLI again as a first-class dispatch mode, with model, reasoning-effort, and timeout flags, that fails closed before dispatch whenever the codex binary is missing.
Dispatch on the fast tier across four models — gpt-5.5 (default), gpt-5.6-luna, gpt-5.6-terra, and gpt-5.6-sol — each with a verified per-model reasoning-effort ceiling (20/20 live cells).

Get the same session guardrails in Codex that Claude has: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, and PreCompact adapters delegate to the shared lifecycle owners, so state, transcript, and compaction stay consistent across runtimes.
Keep Codex agents in lockstep with your canonical OpenCode agents: a checked-in generator derives Codex agent TOMLs from the live agent set and reports stale, missing, or extra adapters.
Track Codex hooks safely via a convergent installer that reconciles entries idempotently, refuses linked-worktree anchors, and fails loudly with actionable JSON when a hook cannot resolve.

title: Canonical cli-external-orchestration hub identity
bullets: `cli-external-orchestration` is now the single canonical hub directory for external CLI dispatch, with full git history preserved through the rename.
Advisor routing and live references now resolve the canonical hub path while keeping `cli-opencode` as the concrete executor packet.

title: Devin returns as a first-class CLI executor
bullets: Dispatch coding, subagent delegation, and cloud handoffs to Cognition's Devin CLI from a new `cli-devin` mode that fails closed when the binary is absent.
Run the framework's full hook lifecycle (session, prompt, tool use, permission, compaction, stop) under Devin, so its spec gates and guardrails behave like Claude's and Codex's.
Use all 13 repository agents as Devin subagents via `.devin/agents/` mirrors, so Devin reviews run on the same profiles as other runtimes.
Plan Devin usage against a pinned live contract covering auth, commands, permission modes, hooks, config, and models, validated by a 20-scenario manual-testing playbook.
Claude and Codex spec-gate hooks also pick up the `firstNonBlankString()` fix, so a blank value can no longer mask the intended first valid string.

title: New cli-cursor executor: delegate work to Cursor CLI
bullets: Delegate coding work to the Cursor CLI (cursor-agent) as a new fourth cli-external-orchestration dispatch mode, with headless print mode, read-only plan/ask modes, and sandbox/approval controls matching the live Cursor CLI contract.
Route to Composer-2.5, Cursor's native model, through a new first-class prompt-craft profile in prompt-models and the executor model registry.

Dispatch safely by default: an unavailable cursor-agent binary never becomes routable (fail-closed), and the mode is guarded against self-invocation and carries its own 19-scenario manual-testing playbook.
Extend spec-gate enforcement into Cursor sessions through new hook adapters that speak Cursor's native hooks.json response format, live-verified to actually block denied tool calls.

title: Pi CLI joined as the 6th executor
bullets: Dispatch the open-source multi-provider Pi CLI as a new fail-closed executor alongside Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor, and Devin.
Drive Pi through a new cli-pi skill packet covering its native skills, prompt templates, extensions, and third-party MCP/sub-agent packages.
Connect Pi to your MCP servers over local stdio transport, with deny-by-default tool gating enforced by Pi core.
A fail-closed model allowlist restricts Pi dispatches to the operator-confirmed 7-model roster, so no unvetted --model value reaches a session.
Pi sessions inherit this framework's scope-lock, spec-folder, quality, and completion-evidence enforcement via bridged native guard cores.

title: Per-mode provider and model catalogs
bullets: Find every CLI mode's providers, models, effort tiers and dispatch shapes in one dedicated providers-and-models.md catalog per mode, instead of hunting through scattered docs.
The hub's smart router now routes all six CLI modes, fixing dispatch coverage that previously only reached three.

Redundant model enumerations in each mode's reference and SKILL.md are trimmed to a compact pointer plus that mode's own defaults and effort mechanics, with cli-cursor's 10-model allowlist kept fully readable inline.
Hub-level docs now point to the per-mode catalogs so the canonical provider/model list lives in exactly one place.

bullets: You can now route a fanout pi lineage to deepseek-v4-flash for latency-optimized turns, where it was previously rejected by the enforced allowlist.
The pi roster was verified live before the change, so the model id you dispatch is confirmed to exist on the pi install.
cli-cursor and cli-devin intentionally remain unchanged because their providers offer no DeepSeek V4 Flash id, and cli-opencode already supported the model.

bullets: Deep-loop cli-pi fan-out can now dispatch to Qwen 3.8 Max, newly added to the enforced model roster.
DeepSeek V4 Flash now dispatches through the subsidized opencode-go "2x usage" gateway by default, while the direct deepseek route still works.
Both cli-pi and cli-opencode docs now cover the opencode-go provider and its dispatch shapes, with each entry backed by live verification.

Projection is privacy-first: it only talks to the hosted or local model provider you choose, and it guarantees an exact-original fallback whenever it can't improve a line.
A compatibility doctor diagnoses your setup and safely falls back to original-only output when anything is misconfigured or unverified.
The capability ships as the sk-communication skill, so you enable it through the skill's own installed package rather than external tooling.

title: Pi Remote Mobile Agent: nine-phase plan approved
bullets: Approved a nine-phase implementation program for a private, Claude-app-style mobile control plane over the Pi CLI, from contract and threat baseline through release verification and rollout.

Shipped executable planning packets for each phase — including relay protocol, auth and tailnet boundary, mobile PWA, approval and remote mutation, and operator runbooks — with product implementation not yet started.

title: Pi remote experience research landed
bullets: Completed a two-lineage deep-research run converging on a typed, redacted, replayable event ledger with a separate authenticated command protocol as the target Pi remote-experience shape.
Delivered P0/P1/P2 recommendations plus 20 open validation questions in research.md to drive the 041 packet amendment.

title: Four new models across CLI orchestration modes
bullets: Dispatch GPT-5.6 Luna Max from cli-cursor (`gpt-5.6-luna-max`, `gpt-5.6-luna-max-fast`) and from cli-devin (`gpt-5-6-luna-max`, `gpt-5-6-luna-max-priority`).
Dispatch DeepSeek V4 Pro Max and V4 Flash Max tiers from cli-devin.
Find GLM 5.3 documented in the opencode-go model catalog for cli-opencode.
Every added model id was verified against the live CLI listings before shipping, so the roster contains no fabricated entries.

title: cli-gemini skill: orchestrate Gemini CLI
bullets: Orchestrate Google's Gemini CLI from Claude Code or OpenCode via the new cli-gemini skill, using a conductor/executor model where your agent plans and Gemini executes.
Smart routing scores 7 task intents and loads only the relevant Gemini docs per request, keeping agent context lean and token use low.
Delegate work to any of 9 Gemini agent types through a built-in routing table, and reuse copy-paste prompt templates for common tasks.

Ask for Gemini help naturally — skill-advisor entries route "use gemini" queries with 0.95 confidence, and discovery covers generation, review, research, architecture, templates, patterns, and agent delegation.

title: New cli-codex skill; cli-gemini simplified to one model
bullets: Run Codex CLI through the same documentation-driven bridge pattern as your other CLI runtimes with the new cli-codex skill.
Find the new Codex bridge skill wherever you already discover CLI skills, since the advisor and README registration surfaces were updated to include it.
Avoid model-choice guesswork when using cli-gemini, which now points to a single canonical model reference.

title: External AIs can now drive Claude Code
bullets: External AI assistants (Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, Copilot) can now delegate tasks to Claude Code CLI through a new cli-claude-code skill that routes requests by intent (deep reasoning, code editing, review, and more).
The skill ships with a full reference library covering Claude Code's CLI flags, 3 model tiers (opus/sonnet/haiku), all 9 delegateable agent profiles, and a comparison against Gemini and Codex CLIs.
Ten prompt-template categories make one-line claude -p invocations available for code generation, review, bug fixing, test writing, documentation, and code transformation.

Unlike cli-gemini and cli-codex, orchestration is reversed: the external AI stays in charge while Claude Code executes, and its default routing favors deep reasoning to match Claude Code's extended-thinking strength.

title: Delegate to GitHub Copilot CLI from any AI assistant
bullets: You can now delegate coding tasks to GitHub's Copilot CLI through a dedicated skill, completing the 4-CLI cross-AI ecosystem alongside cli-gemini, cli-codex, and cli-claude-code.

Copilot's unique value is now accessible: multi-provider model selection (7+ models across Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google), cloud delegation to GitHub infrastructure, and autonomous autopilot execution.
A built-in plan mode and 10 prompt template categories let you drive structured planning, generation, review, and agent-delegation flows out of the box.
Reference material includes model-selection guidance and a 4-way comparison table across all four CLI skills, so you can pick the right executor for each job.

title: CLI bridge skills guard against self-delegation loops
bullets: The CLI bridge skills now stop you from creating a circular loop by delegating to the bridge that targets the very runtime you are running in.
cli-claude-code, cli-gemini, cli-codex, and cli-copilot all share one consistent self-invocation guard, so the anti-delegation guidance reads the same across bridges.
Each guard points you back to the runtime's own native capabilities, making the guidance actionable instead of a bare prohibition.
The change is documentation-only: runtime-awareness remains guidance-driven, with no runtime-detection logic added.

title: Prompt-quality checks and @improve-prompt agent
bullets: Every CLI skill dispatch now enforces a pre-dispatch prompt-quality check and framework-annotated templates, so agents always start from clean, consistent prompts.
High-complexity and compliance-sensitive prompts now route to the new @improve-prompt agent, which applies the full methodology in a fresh, isolated context.
/prompt now supports Inline mode for quick interactive use and Agent mode for deep, fresh-context improvement of complex or isolation-sensitive prompts.

title: Codex CLI gains user-global voice personalization
bullets: Every Codex CLI session now loads a version-controlled voice addendum (symlinked into your home directory) that steers Voice, Tone, and Reasoning Visibility.
Say goodbye to filler openers — Codex now hedges when unsure, shows its reasoning before conclusions, and names trade-offs when several approaches exist.
Codex now states assumptions before acting, surfaces caveats and counterarguments unprompted, and corrects faulty premises with evidence instead of working around them.
Your project-level AGENTS.md framework (gates, scope lock, safety, memory routing) still governs unchanged — the addendum only layers voice on top.
Because the addendum lives in the repo, you can commit and share it; teammates can symlink or copy it into their own ~/.codex/AGENTS.md.

title: New cli-opencode skill: delegate and dispatch to OpenCode
bullets: Dispatch work to the OpenCode CLI from other AI runtimes with the new cli-opencode skill, which covers external delegation, in-OpenCode parallel sessions, and cross-AI handback with full runtime context.
Get productive immediately with 13 ready-to-use prompt templates covering use cases, agent delegation, handback, and refusal scenarios.
Let Skill Advisor surface cli-opencode automatically — it now recommends the skill at 0.95 confidence when you mention delegating to OpenCode, so no manual routing or token boosts are needed.
Keep all five CLI skills consistent, since cli-opencode joins claude-code, codex, copilot, and gemini as a symmetric 0.5-weight sibling so the advisor routes cleanly across them.

title: CLI orchestrators ship manual testing playbooks
bullets: Validate any of the five CLI orchestrator skills end-to-end using ready-made manual testing playbooks — 129 scenarios across 40 categories — without inventing test scenarios yourself.
Shared category numbering across all five playbooks keeps cross-CLI comparison consistent, since the same scenario reads the same in every skill.

New scenarios close earlier surface gaps, adding coverage for the debug, deep-research, deep-review, and orchestrate agents, cost-capping and background execution, and the codex cloud remote-execution mode.
Per-CLI two-letter scenario IDs (CC, CX, CP, CG, CO) keep the simultaneously-shipped playbooks unambiguous in tables and reports.

title: cli-opencode: new default provider and auth pre-flight
bullets: The cli-opencode skill now defaults to the high-capability opencode-go/deepseek-v4-pro --variant high model on the gateway at low cost instead of github-copilot.
The github-copilot provider is no longer documented anywhere in the cli-opencode skill.
A one-shot Provider Auth Pre-Flight runs at session start so missing credentials are detected before dispatching.
When the default isn't logged in, the skill asks you which model to use instead of silently swapping providers, protecting you from unexpected costs and capability mismatches.
The direct DeepSeek API surface (deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro and deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash) remains exactly as before.

title: cli-* skills harmonized with auth pre-flight
bullets: All five cli-* skills now share identical section structure and a Default Invocation block, so guidance reads consistently across providers.
Each cli-* skill now pre-checks provider auth before dispatch, catching missing credentials up front and prompting you to authenticate instead of failing mid-run.
A new Error Handling table maps common CLI failures to concrete fixes, closing the gap in cli-copilot.
Every provider's native flags, agent-routing syntax, and unique capabilities are preserved — nothing existing was removed.

title: mcp-clickup skill removed, ClickUp via Code Mode
bullets: Your ClickUp automation keeps working unchanged — only the local mcp-clickup orchestrator skill was removed, while the ClickUp service wiring through Code Mode (UTCP `clickup` manual, upstream package args, env vars) is preserved.
The skill catalog drops from 22 to 21 skills, and ClickUp-shaped prompts now route to the surviving tooling skills (mcp-code-mode, mcp-chrome-devtools) instead of a ClickUp-specific skill.

All internal references — advisor scoring entries, skill-graph nodes and edges, README and install-guide counts, and manual-testing anchor rows — were pruned, so routing and docs never point at a skill that no longer exists.

title: cli-copilot routing-trace caveats; cli-codex preferred default
bullets: Routing-trace tasks get safer: cli-copilot's SKILL.md now warns when callers consume resource paths literally, a case where it measured 11.1% accuracy versus cli-codex's 66.7%.
sk-doc now recommends cli-codex as the preferred default for routing-trace consumption tasks, backed by per-CLI accuracy figures (cli-codex 66.7% / cli-opencode 47.2% / cli-copilot 11.1%).
Both caveats link to the full stress-matrix evidence, so the cited numbers can be verified rather than taken on faith.

title: cli-copilot removed; use cli-codex instead
bullets: The cli-copilot skill is fully removed from the framework, so any workflow previously dispatching to Copilot must route through cli-codex (gpt-5.5), which was chosen as the replacement because GitHub's Copilot price hike made it the costlier option.

Routing is cleaned up end-to-end: cli-copilot no longer appears in advisor recommendations, skill catalogs, command options, or any of the four runtime agent mirrors, so 'copilot' prompts now resolve to a valid sibling executor like cli-claude-code.

The remaining CLI executors — cli-claude-code, cli-codex, cli-gemini, and cli-opencode — are unchanged and remain fully available, so existing dispatch workflows keep working after you swap the executor.
Configuration and routing surfaces (AGENTS.md, READMEs, install guides, deep-research/deep-review commands) were scrubbed of copilot references so nothing points at the deleted skill.

title: Stdin redirect stops dispatch hangs
bullets: Deep-research and deep-review workflows no longer hang on scripted dispatch: all four YAML assets now append `</dev/null>`, cutting a 12+ minute stall with zero output to a ~16-second run.
A full 10-iteration deep-research loop now completes in about 50 minutes instead of wasting roughly 3 hours across 14 hung attempts.
The cli-opencode skill now documents `</dev/null>` as required for every non-interactive dispatch, with patterns in the README, CLI reference, and prompt templates plus a dedicated changelog.

title: New cli-devin skill: dispatch to Devin for Terminal
bullets: You can now hand coding tasks to Devin's official 'Devin for Terminal' CLI as a peer executor from any assistant — Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, OpenCode, or a raw shell — with a copy-pasteable invocation that defaults to the coding-specialized SWE-1.6 model and a safe 'normal' permission mode.
Devin's unique local-to-cloud handoff is now first-class: a dedicated reference enforces a 5-check operator-confirmation gate before any cloud dispatch, keeping the async escalation human-owned.

The skill ships the same orchestration contract as the other cli-* family members — smart router with self-invocation guard, permission-mode risk taxonomy, and memory handback — so it slots into existing workflows and cross-AI routing without new patterns.
cli-devin is registered as a bidirectional sibling of the four existing cli-* skills, so the skill advisor can now surface and route to it automatically.

title: cli-devin deep-loop iterations: reasoning, tighter writes
bullets: Deep-research and deep-review iterations now use Devin's sequential-thinking tool to reason step by step before acting, making iteration output more deliberate.
Iteration agent configs restrict Devin's file writes to only the two paths each run actually needs, tightening the blast radius of its edits.
Loop starters now watch for tool rejections and treat them as failures instead of letting misbehavior slip through silently.
These effectiveness improvements take effect on future deep-loop runs (cli-devin v1.0.4.0); in-flight runs keep the previous behavior.

title: Data-driven prompt defaults for CLI dispatches
bullets: cli-devin now uses the RCAF (Role/Context/Action/Format) framework as the default for SWE-1.6 dispatches, after it scored 33% higher than the previous STAR baseline in a 42-dispatch optimization run.
Medium-density pre-planning is now the shared recommendation across the sk-prompt CLI card and the sibling CLI prompt-quality cards, since dense pre-planning measurably underperformed.

The RCAF default and its bundle-gate wording are validated across three models (SWE-1.6, deepseek-v4-pro, kimi-k2.6), so the recommended composition is grounded in cross-model evidence rather than anecdote.
Guidance now warns against pairing strict bundle-gate language with verbose constraints, which hurt scores by pushing models toward defensive output.

title: MiniMax: Token Plan default, TIDD-EC prompts

Keep pay-per-token billing by selecting the explicit `minimax` Direct API provider, so both billing modes coexist.
Get higher-quality MiniMax output, because dispatch now uses the TIDD-EC + dense pre-planning prompt framework that won a five-framework benchmark on real MiniMax M2.7.
Use MiniMax 2.7 as a small model wherever the shared model registry and sk-prompt-models surface it.

title: Xiaomi MiMo-V2.5-Pro in cli-opencode and deep skills

Run deep research, deep review, and model-benchmark loops with MiMo-V2.5-Pro or MiniMax token-plan models as executors, since the hard-coded `--agent general` dispatch flag that blocked token-plan providers was removed.
Get the benchmark-verified COSTAR prompt framework (with RACE accepted as a statistical tie) as MiMo's dispatch default, tuned to its strengths rather than MiniMax's guardrail-heavy style.

title: Gemini surface removed
bullets: Framework users can no longer dispatch work to the cli-gemini executor, since the skill, command entries, and executor wiring were removed end-to-end.
Gemini is no longer recognized as a host runtime by hook subsystems and runtime detection, so it disappears from runtime routing and fallback behavior.
Gemini models such as gemini-flash are no longer offered as dispatch or model-benchmark options.
Command docs and catalogs now advertise only supported executors, so operators no longer see Gemini as a selectable option.
The separate external Gemini-CLI binary in your home directory is unaffected and still available for manual use.

title: cli-devin removed; Devin dispatch dropped
bullets: Removed the cli-devin skill entirely, so Devin is no longer an available executor for framework CLI dispatches.
Dropped Devin from executor routing, hooks, and the runtime enum, leaving no stale dispatch paths or dead references.
Re-homed the shared content cli-devin once carried, such as per-model budgets and verification guides, so related tooling keeps working unchanged.

title: Kimi K2.7 Code support and framework defaults
bullets: Kimi K2.7 Code is now a first-class small model in cli-opencode and sk-prompt-models, replacing the retired K2.6 registration.
Kimi K2.7 Code dispatches now default to the empirically winning COSTAR prompt framework, with TIDD-EC as the token-efficient fallback and the old RCAF default retired as weakest.
Known caveat documented: on broad, large-repo dispatches Kimi K2.7 Code can over-explore past a 600s timeout and appear hung (0-byte output) — mitigate with a hard read-cap and a 1200s+ timeout.

title: GLM-5.2: dispatch, vision-to-code, tuned prompts
bullets: Dispatch GLM-5.2 through the Z.AI Coding Plan as a first-class small model, by slug (`zai-coding-plan/glm-5.2`) or the `glm`/`zai` aliases, on its own quota pool.
Get empirically benchmarked GLM-5.2 prompt guidance: COSTAR as primary framework with TIDD-EC as fallback, and RCAF explicitly avoided.
Use GLM-5.2 for vision-to-code — it reads attached images natively via the direct Z.AI Coding Plan API, though `opencode --file` image attachments remain broken for this provider (#20802).
Plan for variable GLM-5.2 latency (6–161s with thinking-on) and rare transient dispatch failures (~1/45), so budget generous timeouts and retry failed cells.

title: Retire cli-codex executor from active routing
bullets: You can no longer dispatch work to the retired cli-codex executor: the skill, its hook trees, and its advisor/commands/matrix/doc/test routes have been removed from active discovery and routing.
Requests for a Codex review now resolve to supported skills (e.g., sk-code-review) instead of a deprecated Codex CLI path.
All historical specs, changelog records, and the archived cli-codex-retired package stay intact, so the retirement is fully auditable and reversible.

Active Codex support now covers only the project-local Codex Desktop bridge (config, context symlinks, and .agents/skills), so Codex Desktop still loads packet and release context after restarting with the project trusted.

title: Hook reference docs relocated to owning trees
bullets: Four hook reference docs now live in the trees that own them, so each doc sits next to the code and config it describes.
All 34 live consumer links were repointed to the new locations and verified, so every existing reference keeps working.
Docs moved with full git rename history preserved, keeping their provenance traceable.

title: Injection bloat reduction: opt-in, shadow-verified
bullets: Limit OpenCode route summaries to three targets with a `+K more` digest and an on-demand reveal, via the new `MK_SKILL_ADVISOR_COMPILED_ROUTE_BOUNDING` flag.
Deduplicate OpenCode system-transform messages on a stable session/message identity so repeat injections ship once, when the opt-in flag is enabled.
Cut the Pi sub-agent dispatch directive from 554 to 165 bytes behind a prototype flag, keeping the full directive as the default while it is validated.
Every bloat-reduction candidate ships shadow-only with byte-parity proofs and delivery receipts, so prompts stay byte-identical until the activation gate flips the flags.

title: Cross-runtime goal hooks now reach Cursor and Pi
bullets: Set an active goal once and it follows you into Cursor and Pi CLI sessions, which now inject the same goal brief into context from one shared goal-state file.
A new goal manage command (set/show/history/clear/complete/pause/resume/doctor) mirrors the OpenCode /goal router across runtimes.
Each runtime gets an honest capability tier: Cursor injects the goal at session start, while Pi injects at input, restores at session start, and observes turn-end verification.
Dispatch auditing now recognizes devin, cursor, pi, and codex invocation shapes, and error-severity dispatch rules now map to blocking instead of warnings.
OpenCode plugins are mirrored into the unified hooks tree as browsability symlinks, so every hook tree and README reflects the real plugin files on disk.

title: Goal-hook playbooks and live cross-runtime validation
bullets: Run goal-hook manual-testing scenarios in any goal-capable CLI runtime (Devin, Cursor, Pi, OpenCode, Claude Code) plus the shared manage CLI, now that playbooks cover each one.
Trust that your active goal actually reaches the model in Pi and Devin, where live runs proved the injection appears verbatim in the model's own output.
Don't expect the active goal in the model's context on Cursor, where the injection is model-invisible by contract and only adapter-level evidence is available.
Note that OpenCode's native mk-goal goal tracking is interactive/TUI-only and can't be driven headless, so verify it via its unit tests or in a session.

title: PI input hook latency cut: in-process advisor
bullets: In the PI runtime, message sends no longer block on a multi-process spawn chain — repeat prompts now resolve from the advisor's in-process cache in about 1-2 ms instead of roughly 1.4 seconds.
Cold prompts drop the adapter/shim process hops and the main-thread freeze, leaving the advisor's own Python recommendation step as the only remaining ~1.3 s tail.
The advisor's 5-minute cache now invalidates correctly, so repeat prompts within the window keep hitting the fast path instead of silently re-paying the cold cost.

title: Spec-gate question no longer repeats on read-only turns
bullets: The SPEC FOLDER QUESTION no longer resurfaces after read-only turns, so you stop getting interrupted by the same prompt when you are not changing files.
When the question does reappear, it is only because your message looks like an answer that failed to bind, so replying with the folder path resolves it.
Every gate option now tells you to reply with the folder path (or skip with E), matching exactly what the gate accepts so a bare choice never leaves it unanswerable.

title: Pi subagent dispatch defaults to native subagents
bullets: On the Pi runtime, subagent dispatch now uses native pi-subagents by default, so skill routing no longer requires an external cli-* executor unless you explicitly request a specific cli-* skill mode.
Pi now denies dispatch-shaped subagent calls that lack an explicit cli-* authorization or an authorized deep-loop executor, closing a subagent-dispatch security gap.

Governor capsule wording is now identical across the Skill Advisor bridge fallback paths and the canonical renderer, with the Fable-5 label kept in sync, so runtime behavior matches regardless of path.
Quoted and wrapper-style executor dispatch is now audited and authorized correctly across runtimes, so printf/echo-style subagent commands resolve to the intended executor.

title: Clean DeepSeek prompt-cache ownership with real observability
bullets: Pi now splits prompt-cache ownership cleanly: a hardened deep-pi extension handles DeepSeek-direct models while pi-cache-optimizer keeps everything else, verified live with zero overlap and no regression.
You get real cache economics instead of promises: deep-pi writes persistent machine-readable stats and reports with measured costs separated from no-cache counterfactual savings.

Deep-pi is now safer and more transparent: previously silent diagnostics surface per session, unrecognized DeepSeek model ids trigger a warning instead of a crash, and cost math is validated before any mutation.
Both extensions run from vendored in-repo copies with a provenance check that reports identity and content drift, so you can verify exactly what code is active.
A research-driven NO-GO kept the install lean: a Reasonix-parity plugin was rejected because the useful caching scope already shipped, saving you a redundant dependency.

bullets: Run every deep-loop workflow — research, review, improvement, and AI council — from a single unified `system-deep-loop` skill instead of two separate packages (the old `deep-loop-workflows` hub and `deep-loop-runtime` backend).
Invoke the deep-loop router agent as `@deep-loop` (renamed from `deep`), so it no longer collides with the `/deep:*` command namespace or the `deep-*` leaf agents.
Give research and review loops a divergent convergence mode that was verified in real 10/10-iteration runs against the skill itself.
A 20-iteration deep review of the unified skill found and fixed 7 confirmed bugs in the deep-research and deep-review runtimes.

title: Smart-routing benchmark: 20-run verification matrix
bullets: Every skill router is now verified by a full 20-run benchmark matrix — 8 children plus both hubs, each scored in deterministic router-replay and live-model modes — so routing regressions are caught before they reach users.

A new circularity meter exposes router overfit: it flagged code-review's perfect deterministic score as having zero live corroboration, and confirmed the four deep-loop routers recall their resources robustly in live runs.

The sk-code parent now enforces a drift-guarded union projection of its children's routers (checked automatically by a test), keeping the two-layer hub's behavior byte-identical while children gain new inline routers for webflow, opencode, and normalized deep-ai-council intent signals.

title: Deep-alignment mode: audit artifacts against skill standards
bullets: Run /deep:alignment to audit your docs, code, designs, or git history against a chosen parent skill's own standards and templates (sk-doc, sk-git, sk-design, sk-code).
Audits are verify-first: every artifact is checked against the authority's real standardSource rather than a hand-rolled checklist.
Document accepted deviations in a per-authority known-deviation list so they stop resurfacing as findings.

Git conformance is checked deterministically (conventional-commit grammar and wt/{NNNN}-name branch naming), while code and design checks pair deterministic rules with a reasoning layer that never judges itself.

title: Deep-review and AI-council robustness fixes
bullets: /deep:review no longer halts when a strategy file arrives with un-numbered or missing section headings — it self-heals and keeps the review running.
/deep:review no longer crashes when writing iteration state — records are now appended deterministically instead of failing on an anchor match.
/deep:ai-council now records execution provenance and the requested-vs-effective route identity for each seat in its persisted output.
/deep:ai-council now rejects executor/model values that collide with reserved executor kinds up front instead of failing later.

title: Benchmark models over the codex transport
bullets: Benchmark any model live over the codex transport side by side with the opencode transport by passing `--executor codex` to the Lane C skill-benchmark, so routing scores compare directly across both executors.
Because codex activation is recorded as unmeasured rather than a miss, codex scores stay fair even though codex emits no `tool_use` event stream.
On the Tier-1 deep-improvement suite the two transports agree within one aggregate point (opencode 86, codex 85, 7 of 9 scenarios identical), so the new transport is measurement-equivalent.

title: Benchmark the OpenCode command surface
bullets: Run the new /deep:command-benchmark launcher to audit the full command corpus on two independent axes: deterministic structural integrity (via a sk-doc-command peer adapter) and behavioral adherence (scenarios DAB-012 through DAB-027 that actually invoke commands).
create-benchmark now authors a fifth family, conformance_benchmark, so you can generate deterministic, oracle-backed conformance benchmark packages for any surface.
Behavior benchmarks gained schema v2 with direct-dispatch evidence and fail-closed postcondition probes while preserving every existing DAB v1 result byte-for-byte.

title: Live-search fan-out and a verifiable deep-loop ledger
bullets: Fan-out dispatches can now run proven live web search, with per-executor tool policy enforced and unsupported combinations rejected before anything dispatches.
Deep-loop runs gain an append-only, tamper-evident event ledger with versioned replay fingerprints, so a run's results can be deterministically replayed and independently verified.
Every phase and mode boundary can now emit a certified receipt and safely recover interrupted external effects without guessing whether they already happened.

title: Graph-Engineering Research Charts Next Deep-Loop Architecture
bullets: Research defined a single coherent design for evolving system-deep-loop into a graph-based agent-loop engine, in which a graph decides eligible work and order, a bounded loop executes each unit, typed evidence stacks, and only the 036 authority plane may authorize protected mutations.

Five reference studies plus the NVIDIA NOOA paper and 12 graph-engineering blogs contributed layered, additive contracts (graph IR, executable belief/evidence and governance-admission checks, and loop/harness deltas) that extend without replacing the existing authority plane.

Every study ran a 20-iteration fan-out deep-research loop with gpt-5.6-sol synthesis and independent DeepSeek V4 Pro verification, closing the program at doctrine level with a shadow-prototype packet as the next evidence step.

title: Improve any agent with a holistic evaluation loop
bullets: Run `/deep:start-agent-improvement-loop` (plus `:auto` and `:confirm` variants) to have an evaluator-first loop propose, score, promote, and roll back improvements to any agent, with repeatability and mirror-drift checks built in.

Agents are now scored across five dimensions — structural integrity, rule coherence, integration consistency, and more — replacing shallow keyword checks (≈15–20% coverage) with holistic integration scanning.

An automatic scanner discovers every surface an agent touches (canonical agent, runtime mirrors, commands, YAML workflows, skills, skill advisor) and derives a scoring profile from the agent itself, so no hardcoded profiles are needed.
Reusable target profiles, fixture catalogs, and a deterministic benchmark runner make agent quality measurable and repeatable.
Breaking: the skill is now named `sk-improve-agent` and the loop command is `/deep:start-agent-improvement-loop`, replacing the old `/speckit:recursive-agent` command.

title: Executable improvement loop with verified discipline
bullets: /deep:start-agent-improvement-loop now runs as a fully executable loop, materializing benchmark fixtures, writing a benchmark-complete report and an agent-improvement-state.jsonl journal, and rendering the latest legal-stop table in its dashboard.
The loop now rejects non-canonical stop reasons (such as benchmarkPlateau) in its journal, so dashboards report only legal stops with all five gates evaluated.
All six agent-discipline stress scenarios now pass end-to-end at the command layer, so the loop's discipline guarantees are verified rather than assumed.

title: Deep-loop command-flow stress-test scaffolding
bullets: Internal QA scaffolding was prepared to stress-test the deep-research and deep-review command flows, extending the methodology already proven on the agent-improvement loop.
No scenarios or stress runs were completed, so this packet ships as draft planning only with no behavior change.

title: Rename sk-improve-agent to deep-agent-improvement
bullets: The agent-improvement skill is renamed from `sk-improve-agent` to `deep-agent-improvement`, aligning it with the `deep-review` and `deep-research` naming family.
All 156 advisor routing phrases were migrated, so prompts like "improve agent" and the `/deep:start-agent-improvement-loop` command continue to work unchanged.
The rename is symbolic-only: no behavior, agent name, or command surface changed, so existing workflows and references are unaffected.

title: Deep AI Council skill with graph-backed decision history
bullets: Convening an AI council now runs through the renamed `deep-ai-council` skill (formerly `multi-ai-council`), so update any existing references to the old name.

Council workflows get a dedicated SQLite-backed graph (`council_graph_*` MCP tools) so decision history can be replayed and queried from saved artifact files instead of re-reading every source document.

Graph-backed council lookups beat the no-graph baseline by up to 13x (e.g., 1 graph call vs 13 file reads for a decision-provenance audit; 12x for disagreement triage), and add structural value like blocker ranking and hot-topic discovery.

A complete manual-testing playbook and one-command test gate now cover every graph tool, query mode, and convergence bucket, including value-comparison scenarios that prove the graph's speed and safety gains.
The council test suite is fully green (43 tests) and now CI-protected so graph behavior stays regression-free.

title: Deep skill evolution: aligned docs, reliable convergence
bullets: deep-review now shows PAUSED/RECOVERING dashboard status when a run is paused or recovering and collapses duplicate findings across dimensions, so its convergence report matches what actually happened.

deep-review's legal-stop model is now consistently documented as nine gates (including the coverage and graphless-fallback gates) across all six reference surfaces, so you can trust the gate list everywhere you read it.

deep-research's convergence and state docs were split into focused references with corrected signal weights (0.30/0.35/0.35) and a resilient smart router, so research stays on-contract and fails over gracefully when resources are missing.
deep-ai-council ships new deep-mode and findings-registry references plus 60 test cases covering previously untested scripts, so council-mode behavior is documented and verified end to end.

the deep-* skills now use a single source-of-truth 10-kind schema allow-list and present-tense evergreen citations instead of a fabricated node kind and transient packet references, keeping their documentation stable across releases.

title: Model-benchmark lane for deep-agent-improvement
bullets: Benchmark any model or prompt framework with the new /deep:start-model-benchmark-loop command, which reuses the deep-agent-improvement loop, convergence, and state machinery (~90% of the plumbing).
Existing agent-improvement runs behave exactly as before: the /deep:start-agent-improvement-loop command resolves the lane automatically and only asks when genuinely ambiguous.
Choose pattern or an opt-in 5-dimension scorer and noop/mock/llm graders to fit each benchmark run.
The deep-agent-improvement skill now presents agent-improvement and model-benchmark as two co-equal lanes, so the correct workflow and guidance load automatically.
Deep-loop restarts no longer leave empty research/review archive directories in spec packets, and a latent loop-host scorer/grader forwarding defect is fixed.

title: Skill-benchmark lane and deep-improvement rename
bullets: Run the new skill-benchmark lane via `/deep:start-skill-benchmark-loop` to measure whether a skill is actually discovered, routed to, and used effectively by an AI in real scenarios.
`deep-agent-improvement` is now `deep-improvement`, and it gained a third evaluation lane for benchmarking skills themselves (legacy prompt phrases still resolve via back-compat aliases).

Skill benchmarks score routing accuracy, unprompted reference/asset discovery, efficiency, and real usefulness — four dimensions deterministically, plus an optional live skill-on/off task-outcome ablation.
The `sk-code` skill is now benchmarkable end-to-end and routes more efficiently thanks to surface-aware, language-aware routing (verified with no routing recall regression).

title: Parallel fan-out groundwork
bullets: Deep-loop gained internal building blocks for opt-in parallel multi-executor fan-out: validated fan-out config parsing plus a concurrency-capped worker pool with a JSONL status ledger, with the single-executor path left byte-identical.
The planned follow-ons — a per-iteration model schedule and a remediation pass for 14 review findings — are design-documented only and not yet shipped.

title: Deep-context loop shipped and hardened
bullets: Run /deep:start-context-loop to automatically gather codebase context into a reuse-first Context Report via a 4th deep loop with cross-executor agreement convergence.
Launch the context loop from OpenCode, Claude Code, or Codex and pick Native (free, in-process) or Custom executors — Native is the new default.
Point a /deep:* run at a spec folder by naming its path in the scope, and the run now lands inside that folder instead of a standalone directory.
Every /deep:* command now starts with two un-skippable gates: an orchestrator check plus a blocked-until-complete setup phase.
The context loop inherits the same durability guarantees as the other deep loops, including atomic state, state-file repair, and loop locking.

title: Deep-skill workflows now lock to the plan-named command
bullets: When a plan names a specific command, agent, or workflow, the assistant must now use exactly that workflow instead of improvising a manual substitute.
The rule extends to every deep skill (context, research, review, council, improvement), so plan-named deep loops always run through their real command.
The fix is stored as cross-runtime feedback memory, so the lesson surfaces automatically at prompt time in any runtime instead of repeating a one-off correction.

title: Per-executor Claude config-dir routing
bullets: Route an individual cli-claude-code fan-out seat through its own Claude config directory (e.g. ~/.claude-account2) so a Fable 5 account override never leaks to Codex, OpenCode, native seats, or the parent process.
Set the per-lineage account with --config-dir=PATH on start-review-loop and start-research-loop, or via the configDir executor field, instead of overriding globally.
~ paths are expanded and injected as CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR only for cli-claude-code lineages, composing with the existing CLAUDE_ allowlist and per-replica state isolation.

title: Deep-review optimization keeps baseline unchanged
bullets: The @deep-review agent was run through a 5-iteration improvement loop via cli-copilot and kept as-is, since every candidate scored at the 100/100/100/100/100 ceiling with zero delta.
An operator review stays open so the best-of-5 synthesis candidate can still be promoted if its qualitative changes carry value the structural scorer cannot see.

title: Deep-research skill audit keeps baseline
bullets: Ran a 5-iteration improvement loop on the @deep-research skill covering discipline hardening, concision, edge cases, integration, and best-of synthesis, with every candidate scoring 100 across all five quality axes.

The loop kept the existing baseline (delta 0) — matching the known ceiling for already-mature agents — so no changes were promoted; any worthwhile ideas from the synthesis candidate are left to operator review.

title: Deep-loop skills renamed to deep-review and deep-research
bullets: The deep-loop skills are now consistently named `deep-review` and `deep-research` across every surface — folders, OpenCode internals, runtime mirrors, root docs, and configs — instead of the old `sk-deep-*` IDs.
The skill advisor now routes deep-research and deep-review prompts to the right skill reliably, with tuned loop keywords so iterative review and research passes dispatch correctly.
The skill-graph schema now accepts the `deep-loop` family end-to-end, so the family rename is valid across metadata, compiler validation, and the SQLite graph.
The rename was swept across 1,514 active references with no stale old-name hits remaining outside known exclusions.

title: Rename @improve-agent to @deep-agent-improvement
bullets: The agent-invocation handle is now @deep-agent-improvement, aligning it with the deep-agent-improvement skill and the /deep:* command family for a consistent naming system.
Update any references to the old @improve-agent handle across your prompts and skill internals; the rename touched all four runtime mirrors (opencode, Claude, Gemini, Codex).
Your existing /deep:start-agent-improvement-loop command still works unchanged — the slash command is intentionally left as-is, mirroring the /prompt family pattern.
This is a pure semantic rename with no behavior change: only naming shifted, with historical references preserved verbatim.

title: deep-review :auto non-interactive setup bypass
bullets: `/deep:start-review-loop:auto` now resolves setup non-interactively from pre-bound answers, arguments, and defaults when inputs are bound or defaultable, so autonomous runs skip the interactive question block.
You can pre-bind setup inputs directly in the prompt body using the documented `PRE-BOUND SETUP ANSWERS:` block, which takes precedence over `$ARGUMENTS` flags.
When only a single field is genuinely ambiguous, the command asks one narrow clarification instead of the full question list.
Missing required inputs now fail fast with a named-missing-inputs error and a non-zero exit instead of hanging.
The `:confirm` mode keeps its existing consolidated question flow unchanged.

title: Merge duplicate deep-review findings across dimensions
bullets: Deep-review synthesis now merges the same finding surfaced by multiple review dimensions into one entry with a combined dimensions list instead of reporting it repeatedly.

Each finding gets a content_hash derived from its file, line range, finding type, and normalized description, so near-identical findings with slightly different titles are no longer treated as separate duplicates.
Existing review state files keep working without migration, since findings without the new hash still match through the file:line + title fallback.

title: Mutation dedup for improvement runs
bullets: Improvement runs no longer re-propose mutations that were already tried or exhausted, because each mutation now gets a stable sha256 signature recorded in mutation-coverage.json.
Signatures include the target section, so genuinely different mutations to different sections are still proposed.
Set DEEP_AGENT_IMPROVEMENT_SKIP_DEDUP=1 to intentionally retry a previously tried mutation, with full history still recorded for future runs.
Skipped mutations carry an EXHAUSTED-FROM: iter-NNN reason so you can see where each dead end came from.
Existing coverage files without signatures keep working via the old dimension/mutationType key fallback.

title: Six deep-loop READMEs rewritten in plain narrative voice
bullets: Deep-loop skill READMEs now lead with each skill's value in plain narrative prose before explaining mechanics, so you can pick the right loop without decoding jargon.
Outdated facts that contradicted the real skills—stale version lines and drifted script/test counts—were dropped from all six READMEs.
Each README now opens with a quick start, from the deep-ai-council planning model and six lenses to the deep-research convergence stop signal and fresh-context review passes.

deep-review's README documents the release-readiness verdict (PASS, CONDITIONAL or FAIL) that routes your next command, and deep-loop-runtime is now presented as the shared foundation the five deep loops ride.

title: Multi-AI Council durable write protocol
bullets: Council deliberations now persist as durable ai-council artifacts through a scoped writer library covering configs, strategies, state, seats, deliberations, critiques, and reports.
Every council artifact write is recorded in an audit trail with sha256 checksums, and a failed round can be rolled back into failed/ without losing its supersede markers.
The Multi-AI Council agent now resolves the target packet path before any deliberation and must persist outputs before claiming completion, enforced by five gates across all four runtime mirrors.
Council runs gain v1.1 state metadata with routed memory-save payloads and advisor checks so results feed downstream memory correctly.

title: Dedicated deep-review command with durable, resumable loops
bullets: Review work is now a standalone `/speckit:deep-review` command and `sk-deep-review` skill, replacing the old `/speckit:deep-research:review` subcommand so you can run iterative code audits independently of research.
Deep-research state now lives in a durable `research/` packet root and review output (including the final report) in a `review/` folder, replacing scratch storage and auto-migrating legacy artifacts.

Every deep research and deep review loop now records a named stop reason, passes a legal-stop gate, and carries a resume cursor, so interrupted or finished sessions continue deterministically instead of silently ending.
Loop observability improved with append-only journals and dashboards showing timing, tool/token histograms, convergence trends, and stop-decision drill-downs.

title: Deep-loop skills consolidated into one workflow skill
bullets: The five deep-loop skills (deep-research, deep-review, deep-context, deep-improvement, deep-ai-council) were merged into one deep-loop-workflows skill with five modes, so a single skill now covers all loop workflows.
All /deep:* commands and the deep-loop agents keep their names and behavior, just repointed to the merged skill, so existing workflows continue unchanged.
The skill advisor now routes deep-loop prompts to the single merged skill plus a concrete mode, giving more precise routing instead of five flat skills.
Framework docs now describe the two-skill deep-loop model, and the merged skill ships at version 1.0.0 with per-mode changelog history preserved.
The old five deep-* skills were deleted after validation, so references to them no longer resolve.

title: Deep-loop runtime hardening and convergence signals
bullets: State writes are now cheaper and safer: unchanged content is skipped via serialize-diff, JSONL merges run under lock with dedupe, and a deferred writer coalesces redundant saves.
Cancellation and concurrency are more reliable: abortable chunked sleeps, legal lifecycle transition guards, and heartbeat-refreshed single-flight loop locks collapse duplicate acquires.
Loop health is more observable: convergence score-delta signals, fixed-rate slot-overrun accounting, and byte-offset log regions surface per-iteration timing and drift.

title: Reliable deep-loop routing and dispatch for GPT-backed agents
bullets: Deep-loop commands now route by explicit, registry-backed route identity, so GPT-backed agents resolve the correct mode and target agent up front instead of inferring it from prose.
A new dispatch guard flags (and can block) Task dispatches whose declared mode contradicts the route registry, catching mis-routed deep work before it runs.
Every /deep:* command replaced its unanswerable self-assessment gate with an evidence-based dispatch-context check, removing a hard-block that could stop capable agents from proceeding.
Route-proof validation now rejects schema-valid but semantically wrong-mode iteration artifacts, so an off-route deep-loop result can no longer pass as valid.
The ai-council agent is now subagent-only: direct top-level invocation is rejected with a fallback to the default agent (breaking).

title: /goal: persistent per-session goals
bullets: Set a per-session `/goal` that is injected into every turn as guidance until it is met.
Check goal status, token and time usage, and verifier evidence with `/goal status`.
Goals automatically stop once they hit their configured token budget.
Goals auto-complete only when a strict verifier confirms the objective is met, with redacted evidence shown in status.
Your raw goal text is rewritten into a deterministic execution brief for more precise direction.

title: Behavioral benchmarks for all five deep-loop skills
bullets: Every deep-loop skill — deep-review, deep-research, deep-context, deep-ai-council, and deep-improvement — now ships a behavior benchmark package that scores executors against realistic, often vague user prompts.
A shared harness ran ~120 scored runs across five modes and three executors, measuring sub-agent delegation, stalls, and latency against a Claude baseline.
Findings show reasoning effort drives delegation integrity: gpt-fast-high never silently absorbs a sub-agent's role, while gpt-fast-med stalls or fakes delegation.
The benchmarks expose a repeated Gate-3 documentation halt by GPT executors across all four command surfaces and a ranked remediation backlog (P0).
Each sub-skill README now links to its own benchmark, so results are discoverable from the skill they test.

title: Deprecate standalone /deep:context
bullets: /deep:context no longer runs a live context loop — it now redirects with replacement guidance and writes no context artifacts.
Your codebase-context behavior is preserved as replacement snapshot capabilities inside /deep:research and /deep:review.
Starting a context loop is now rejected cleanly, while historical context artifacts still parse and remain test-covered.
Deprecated agent stubs, docs, and mirrors are cleaned up so they guide you to the replacement instead of staying discoverable as dead surfaces.

title: Deep-loop runtime reliability, dedup, and continuity
bullets: Deep-research loops no longer crash on the first reduce, because freshly copied strategy templates now carry the anchor markers the reducer needs to fold cross-iteration state cleanly.

Fan-out merge results are now deterministic and order-invariant, so the same findings merge byte-identically regardless of arrival order, with an opt-in near-duplicate dedup that collapses restated points while keeping the strongest severity.

Failed fan-out runs recover instead of losing work: transient failures retry within a durable budget, orphaned lineages get flagged, and an explicit --require-existing-state gate keeps resuming a run distinct from starting fresh.

Deep-review continuity carries forward open questions into the next iteration and derives Next Focus from that thread, and the session-id handoff across review/context/research workflows is now pinned by tests.

The fan-out lag warning now fires only on a genuine stall rather than healthy pool backpressure, and graph-novelty auditing plus progress heartbeats are available for STOP-input corroboration (all default-off pending benchmark calibration).

title: Rust rewrite of skill advisor researched
bullets: Mapped whether the skill-advisor backend's ~51K LOC TypeScript deserves a Rust rewrite, so any engineering commitment is grounded in cited evidence instead of assumptions.
Split the question across the scoring/ranking core and the embeddings/vector/serving half, so each can be evaluated independently.
Each half runs a 16-round deep-research pass that ends in a ranked recommendation: full rewrite, targeted native module, sidecar, or do-not-rewrite.

title: Contain stray state directories, audit advisor
bullets: Stops runtime writers from planting nested .opencode state trees and cleans up the 40 already leaked into the workspace.
Dispositions the nine findings from the advisor-surface audit so the advisor code stays healthy and maintainable.

title: Codex skill advisor Node ABI startup fix
bullets: Codex sessions now finish MCP startup instead of aborting, because the skill advisor launches on the Node runtime (ABI 141) its native SQLite module requires.
Memory and code-mode MCP servers keep their proven Node 22 and Node 24 pins, so the fix changes only the advisor's runtime.
The other MCP servers were healthy all along and merely skipped after the advisor interrupted startup, as confirmed by independent handshakes.

title: Safer routing defaults and a much faster advisor
bullets: Passing `--threshold` no longer silently disables uncertainty guarding, and you can opt into confidence-only behavior explicitly with `--confidence-only`.
Command bridges are deprioritized for natural-language prompts unless you use an explicit slash command, reducing false-positive routing.
Warm-path routing is roughly 25x faster thanks to in-process caching and frontmatter-only parsing.
You can run the advisor in batch mode over a file or stdin with `--batch-file` and `--batch-stdin` to cut subprocess overhead.

title: Skill router recalibrated for reliable routing
bullets: The skill advisor graph was reindexed and validated so prompt-to-skill routing runs from a fresh, live baseline.
Phrases like "save the file I'm working on" no longer misfire into memory-save routing, while "preserve everything we figured out today" now routes there reliably.
Testing-playbook creation prompts now route to the dedicated testing-playbook command instead of generic documentation.
Ambiguous "what's wrong with my code" prompts now route toward code-review instead of plain implementation work.
Command and skill aliases (such as /speckit:deep-review and spec_kit:deep-review) are canonicalized so routing matches capabilities consistently.

title: Sharper ambiguity detection for close skill matches
bullets: Skill Advisor now flags a match as ambiguous when either the top result's score or its confidence is within 0.05 of the runner-up, so near-ties surface as uncertain instead of a single confident pick.
Confidence-tied recommendations that were previously collapsed into one confident match now stay visible as an ambiguity cluster.
The score-margin behavior is unchanged, so clearly superior recommendations are still selected decisively.

title: Graph-aware skill advisor routing, now standalone
bullets: Skill recommendations are now graph-aware, using compiled skill relationships, intent signals, and family affinity to boost the most relevant matches and penalize conflicting ones.
A native TypeScript advisor scorer replaced the legacy pipeline, keeping results consistent with the old behavior through compatibility shims.
The skill advisor now runs as a standalone MCP server exposing stable advisor_recommend, advisor_status, and advisor_validate tools.
A metadata quality sweep cleaned duplicated descriptions and trigger phrases across cli-* and deep-loop skills so adjacent skills are told apart more accurately.

title: Skill routing now uses semantic similarity
bullets: Skill recommendations now blend semantic similarity with keyword and author signals, so prompts that describe intent instead of naming a skill land on the right recommendation more often.
Per-skill description embeddings are cached in the skill graph and refreshed on scan, keeping semantic scoring fast and current without repeated embedding work.
advisor_recommend and advisor_validate now accept an explicit workspaceRoot and report the effective threshold and state they used, making cross-workspace calls predictable.
Corpus-driven sweeps confirmed a conservative 0.05 semantic weight that lifts intent-described routing without regressing today-correct recommendations.

title: Smarter Skill Advisor Routing, Hooks, and Setup
bullets: Skill recommendations are now markedly more accurate — e.g. agent-scoring queries route to the agent-improvement skill at 0.95 confidence instead of misrouting to prompt-improvement at 0.77.
Search and reranking were retuned (balanced semantic/keyword/graph fusion weights, a higher rerank minimum) for cleaner, better-scored results.
The router is safer and self-checking: five stale route references were fixed, routing is validated statically, and unknown queries now return an explicit UNKNOWN instead of silently falling back.
A new /doctor:skill-advisor command lets you analyze your skills, optimize advisor scoring tables, and re-index the skill graph without touching internal config.
Advisor hooks now surface proactive skill suggestions on every prompt in Claude, Gemini, Copilot, and Codex runtimes, with fast cached briefs and a fail-open no-op on any error.

title: Skill advisor hardening: reliability, hooks, quality
bullets: Skill recommendations now flow into Codex and Devin sessions through native startup and prompt hooks, matching the experience Claude users already get.
The advisor stays responsive under load: concurrent identical prompts share a single bridge call, payloads are size-capped, and the cache evicts its oldest entries.

Recommendation scoring got sharper: suppressive conflict signals now survive to fusion, token-stuffed prompts are resisted, tied candidates resolve by ranking score, and fallback briefs render consistently.
The advisor now fails open when unavailable and only claims routing readiness once live telemetry records real reads, eliminating stale-context silence and false readiness.

title: Skill-advisor docs aligned with hook-first workflow
bullets: Skill-advisor docs now present hook invocation as the primary Gate 2 path, with the direct Python CLI kept as a documented fallback for diagnostics and scripted checks.
The tool surface is now described consistently everywhere as 8 public tools plus 1 internal trusted-caller tool, and the opencode.json registration comment matches that count.
New operator references cover the full skill-graph query API with worked examples, advisor validation baselines, daemon lease handling, and drift detection and reconciliation.
The four legacy hook READMEs now carry a 90-day deprecation banner, pointing users to the hook surface as the canonical path.
Spec-kit documentation no longer describes skill-advisor or code-graph internals, so each framework skill's docs cover only its own scope.

title: Sharper Skill Advisor routing for commands and reviews
bullets: Explicit slash commands like /memory:save now route to their owning skill (system-spec-kit) instead of a bridge alias.
Code-edit requests without an explicit CLI invocation now route to sk-code, while broad low-information prompts abstain instead of guessing.
OpenCode users now get an Advisor: brief through the plugin bridge's native compat route instead of a silent python fallback.
Deep-loop colon syntax like :review:auto routes to deep-review, while bare "auto review" stays on sk-code-review.
All 50 regression cases now pass in both the TypeScript and Python scorers, restoring the two implementations to behavioral parity.

title: Pluggable embedder stack for skill-advisor
bullets: Choose from six embedder options for skill-advisor — including jina-embeddings-v3, nomic-embed-text-v1.5, mxbai-embed-large-v1, and bge-m3 — instead of being locked to one model.
Swap the active embedder with a single operator call, setActiveEmbedder(db, name, dim), backed by a documented step-by-step runbook with rollback.
A new "Choosing an embedder" install-guide section explains every registered option, the swap mechanism, and how device selection behaves (Ollama Metal/CUDA/CPU, llama-cpp fallback).
Duplicate daemon launches no longer leave zombie skill-advisor processes behind, thanks to a launcher-owned PID guard.

title: Skill-Advisor CLI Fallback and Reliability
bullets: Skill recommendations now keep working when the advisor MCP daemon is down, because prompt-time hooks fail open to a warm-only CLI fallback in Claude, Codex, and the OpenCode bridge.
You get identical skill suggestions from the new 9-command CLI and the MCP server, since the CLI schemas are byte-identical to the tool definitions.

title: Skill doc triggers route advisor matches
bullets: The skill advisor now harvests title, description, trigger phrases, and tier from each skill's references/assets docs (84 of ~355 today) into the skill graph when SPECKIT_ADVISOR_DOC_TRIGGERS=true, so doc-level detail that used to be dead metadata can influence routing.

Doc phrase matches are capped (top-3 docs per skill, tier-weighted, 0.45 contribution ceiling) so doc volume can't outrank curated skill phrases, and the recommendation response can point users at the exact file to open via an optional matchedDocs field.

title: Advisor resilience, observability, and spec-folder hygiene
bullets: Ask the advisor why a skill was recommended: `includeAttribution` now returns a prompt-safe `why_recommended` breakdown (dominant lane, top lanes, matched feature categories) without exposing your prompt text.
Get vector-lane health without reading logs: `advisor_status` now reports the active embedder, vector coverage, dimension-mismatch flag, and last refresh timestamp on demand.

Advisor sessions no longer fail silently when the socket goes dead: the launcher detects failed deep probes, reaps stale child processes under a lock, and respawns a replacement that still answers your request.
Advisor state no longer leaks into your spec folders: the workspace-root resolver hoists out of any `specs/` tree, and 23 stray `.advisor-state` directories were cleaned up.

title: Advisor docs aligned to canonical contract
bullets: Skill routing is now more reliable because all 15 system-skill-advisor reference docs carry the canonical frontmatter contract (importance tier, context type, trigger phrases).

The tier system now matches its own rules: formal contract and compatibility-guarantee docs sit at important while operational runbooks, cookbooks and baselines sit at normal, so advisor ranking reflects true authority.
Search triggers are more distinctive, with generic one-word phrases like "skill graph database" replaced by specific multi-word phrases that match cleanly.

title: Stall detection and dispatch rule enforcement
bullets: Deep-loop research and review runs now fail loudly when they stall or die abnormally, instead of silently reporting success.
Skill CLI dispatches are now checked against hard rules, so you get a warning before running a misconfigured invocation.
Stall and abort events are surfaced to stderr, making hung or orphaned runs visible in your logs.

title: More reliable, honest skill-advisor scoring and routing
bullets: Skill-advisor routing now comes from one metadata-driven resolver shared by both the TypeScript and Python engines, so executor delegation is consistent and orchestrator-style requests land on the right skill instead of hardcoded boosts.
On audit prompts the advisor can no longer recommend itself, because the self-recommendation penalty now also demotes the skill-advisor alias, not just the canonical id.
Advisors whose vector embeddings are stale now fail closed and surface a stale-vector warning instead of serving untrusted or empty matches.
A degraded scoring lane is now excluded from confidence and abstention calculations, and the degraded condition is explained in output instead of silently distorting scores.

The advisor now resolves its workspace root deterministically rather than from the working directory, so state always lands in the canonical .advisor-state location and stray nested state folders are cleaned up.

title: Rust-rewrite feasibility research
bullets: Opened a 20-round deep-research pass to decide whether, where, and how the TypeScript backend (~244K LOC) would benefit from a Rust rewrite, grounded in code-referenced evidence rather than assumptions.

The research answers three linked questions — what Rust would improve, what new features it unlocks, and what stays hard or impossible in TypeScript — and converges on a ranked recommendation: full rewrite, targeted native module, or do-not-rewrite.

It separates the genuinely CPU-bound compute core (fusion, reranking, embeddings, indexing) from the glue sitting in front of already-native primitives (sqlite-vec, better-sqlite3, transformers, web-tree-sitter), so only work with real payoff is considered.
This phase writes no Rust and leaves the current backend untouched — the TypeScript source is read-only research material until the recommendation warrants a later PoC.

The generator is workflow-aware rather than a hard gate, so the quality of the resulting changelog still depends on the quality of the packet's own documents.
